Arg-Ôrdstun (H76)

Survey region (English rating-table region): Serpentspine.

In one sentence: Open a Diamond Dwarven hold sealed for six thousand years and polish its stubborn old hegemon into a gem empire ruling the Serpentspine.

Storytelling: Very high | Mission-tree length: Very long (48 direct H76 missions, across two acts) | Mission-tree update: formally released in the 2024 update; the current local mission file was modified on 2026-07-09 and supports v1.37.5.0 | Uniqueness: Very high | Tedium: Medium-high | Early pressure: Medium-high | Expansion capacity: High

Identity and history

Arg-Ôrdstun (H76) is not a ruin waiting for a Dwarven adventurer company to reclaim: in 1444, the Diamond Dwarves still hold their hold, follow Ancestor Worship, and are ruled by Ardeginn XXII Whiteforged. The country history script gives her a reformer personality while preserving the traces of the Dwarven Remnant and the stagnation disaster. Arg-Ôrdstun was once hegemon of the western Serpentreach holds; diamond mining, the lapidary guild, and combative nobles shaped it. The old War of the Bloody Gem over the Dwarven high-kingship left its dispute with Amldihr and Rubyhold unresolved.

A long Orcish siege changed everything. The offline Wiki records Queen Sigrid using mines, shafts, and traps to repel the invaders, then issuing a decree forbidding Diamond Dwarves from leaving the hold. It preserved the population but locked the country into isolation and privilege. The Wiki entries disagree on the exact opening year of the ancient invasion; “survival in isolation” is a better description of the 1444 position than a forced precise date. Ardeginn’s opening of the gates is not the completion of reform but a war against the traditionalists controlling the nobles, lapidaries, and temples.

National story and campaign arc

The first act begins with repealing the old decree. The Diamond Dwarves leave the hold and face a Serpentspine and surface that have become unfamiliar, repair the neighbouring Glass and Marble holds, and reconnect with Cannorian merchants. Arg-Ôrdstun must reclaim lost ground while answering a harder question: can a realm that once dominated the region still act while clans, assemblies, and guilds pull it in different directions? As missions advance, traditionalist resistance, gem trade, and territorial recovery become entangled. After the western Serpentreach is recovered and the capital has grown, a country flag unlocks the second act without changing Tag.

The second act turns ambition toward the Dwarven world. Arg-Ôrdstun contests the middle routes and the old imperial throne, establishes control over other holds, and turns diamond craft into deeper excavation, military, and trade advantages. It also wages a cross-mountain commercial war against Rubyhold: when gem output becomes excessive, the mission story allows artificial scarcity, tariffs, and exclusive trade to preserve its position. The ending is not predetermined history in 1444 but an alternate future driven by the player—a diamond regime that sees itself as harder and more centralised than old Aul-Dwarov.

Core mechanics

  1. From “roughness” to “lustre”: the reformist government begins with 100 roughness; high roughness harms reform progress, legitimacy, and prestige. Stabilising the country, completing agendas, and mission events can lower it, but the process brings traditionalist events and rebellions. At zero, events switch to lustre reform. Lustre accumulates over time and can be spent at a cost of 50 points on three actions: lowering autonomy, pacifying rebels and estates, or strengthening wartime resilience. These are not free buttons available from the opening.
  2. Lapidary guild and trade war: the country begins by reorganising the Gromdhal Lapidary Guild and reopening diamond, glass, and marble production networks. Later it must handle prices, trade access, and Rubyhold competition; commercial victory and territorial conquest run in parallel rather than replacing each other.
  3. Two-act missions and hegemony: all current 48 direct missions belong to H76. Representative western-recovery missions set the second-act flag and refresh the tree; political focus then reaches toward the middle Serpentspine and Amldihr. The count is the number of mission entities, not a claim that all 48 appear simultaneously in 1444.
  4. Diamond craft and deep holds: the missions connect great mines, improved excavation, hold repairs, and precision instruments into an economic and military loop. Some late-story passages give legendary gems bolder uses; these are post-mission developments, not opening abilities.

Staged play

The opening is not a homeless adventurer company, but it does not offer stable freedom. Handle Dwarven Remnant stagnation and the resistance of nobles and guilds, secure finances and hold defences, then push into the western Serpentreach. Falling roughness does not necessarily make the situation immediately easy: the old order may retaliate through rebels and estate costs. A 2024 player critique said this pacing and the colonisation bottleneck slowed the early game; comments included players who enjoyed the campaign while barely managing roughness. This is a version-bound experience split.

After recovering neighbouring holds, roads, mining, and surface trade fund expansion. In the middle and late game, contest the passages, crown gems, and other Dwarven lands, using lustre actions to manage autonomy, rebels, and war exhaustion. A detailed 2025 guide recommends consolidating west before expanding east, but its author used submods and save-scumming; it is not the sole vanilla route.

Formation relations and end state

H76 already exists in 1444. A generic decision can also allow a qualifying Dwarven adventurer company to form H76 if it does not exist; that decision does not reproduce Ardeginn’s opening history, so this article’s continuous story uses native H76. Another generic option forms Aul-Dwarov (I24) and changes Tag. Arg-Ôrdstun’s exclusive story can decline that generic formation, retain H76, and later rename the country Szetur Ôrdstunov through an event. Renaming is not formation of I24, and I24 content must not be counted among H76’s 48 missions.

Personality and recommendation

The v2.1 personality coordinates are Expansion 84/100 | Autocracy 75/100 | Magic↔Artifice 30/100 (100 = magic, 0 = artifice; theme intensity 48/100) | Pluralism 40/100.

The v2.1 values result is Neutral (61/100) with a mixed trajectory. Ending isolation, weakening hereditary privilege, and rebuilding holds have public value; later commercial monopoly, forceful suppression of competitors, and Dwarven hegemony keep the result neutral rather than good.

Recommended for players who enjoy Dwarven revival, internal political resistance, gem economics, and two-act long-form expansion. If you want an immediately efficient government, peaceful tall play, or no need to handle stagnation, rebellion, colonisation, and multi-front war, polishing this shining hold will be punishing.

Evidence boundary

The current Tag, Chinese display name, missions, government mechanics, and formation relations come from the local Mod and translation Mod; the offline Wiki supplies the background of the War of the Bloody Gem and the Diamond Queen’s sealed hold. A 2024 official development diary records design intent, not a replacement for current values. Two player posts represent version-specific play experiences; intermediate borders in the community historical map remain projections and are not treated as inevitable campaign history.

National ideas (reference appendix)

The following reproduces the current local national-idea text and script effects. Traditions apply when the idea set is adopted, the seven ideas unlock in sequence, and the ambition applies after all seven ideas. Only national ideas are listed; racial, government, and mission rewards are not mixed into the numbers. Formation ideas are not automatically stacked with the old set. Idea descriptions may recall history or describe a future ideal and do not automatically represent events already completed in 1444.

Arg-Ôrdstun (H76) — Diamond Ideas

Traditions: Diamond Traditions

Effects: Production efficiency: +15%; Shock damage: +10%.

Idea 1: Great Clast Shafts of Arg-Ôrdstun

A journey through the cavernous hold of Arg-Ôrdstun will no doubt reveal several massive, circular shafts piercing the rock to depths unseen: These are kimberlite veins of ancient, solidified magma that resemble tall, vertical pipes and from which diamonds are mined. One can hear the grinding of great lifts in the heavy air along the edge of the shafts and see the dozens of bridges, both makeshift and grand, that cleave the empty space between the clast shafts. Bustling workshops ring the shafts, taking advantage of a complex pulley system to move goods up and down.

Once the veins were cleared out, enterprising dwarves quickly took advantage of the existing mining infrastructure to build their homes and shops.

Effects: Development cost: -10%.

Idea 2: Formation of the Gromdhal Lapidary Guild

The lapidaries of Arg-Ôrdstun were infamous for stubbornly feuding with each other, to perfect their diamond gemcutting techniques to gain the favour of their ruler. The formation of the state-sponsored Gromdhal guild however aimed to remedy that, consolidating and redirecting the energies of the Diamond artisans outward. Their famous diamonds reached all of the ends of the Dwarovar, adorning jewellery and ceremonial weaponry to complement the crafts of other holds.

Effects: Yearly inflation reduction: +0.05%; National tax modifier: +10%.

Idea 3: Lightflare Armour

First used millennia ago during the endless skirmishes against the sun hating cave goblins, lightflare armour is embedded with dozens of diamonds. This diamond-studded armour was carefully crafted and warded to reflect light directly into the eyes of any would-be ambushers from the dark of the caverns, sowing discord in the ranks of enemies foolish enough to charge into a frontline of dwarves standing resolute with lightflare armour. Later generals developed offensive tactics with this practice relevant against all races they encountered, keeping this ancient and simple technique relevant.

Effects: Discipline: +5%.

Idea 4: The Aegis of the Serpentreach

Faceted so masterfully that the massive gem's very center seems to draw in and pulsate with light, the Aegis was the crown jewel of the Arg-Ôrdstun. It is said to have strange mental effects on those who gaze for too long into its depths. Whether those effects are real or imagined, the presence of the diamond has served the leaders of Arg-Ôrdstun well in many diplomatic negotiations. As the clamour for a united dwarven empire grew and Arg-Ôrdstun pledged support, the Aegis was forfeited to adorn the Dwarovkron, only for them to seek to wear the crown in the future themselves.

Effects: Prestige: +1; Monthly splendor: +1.

Idea 5: Diamond Hegemony

Our hold once held sway over the entirety of the Serpentreach, from the deepwoods bulwark of Verkal Skomdihr, to the great marble mausoleums of Shazstundihr, and even to the rebellious, blackened halls of Gor Bûrad. Hegemony over the holds was a priority in order to challenge the absolute rule of Amldihr, as our natural right extend not only to the Serpentreach but also to Aul-Dwarov.

Effects: Core-creation cost: -15%.

Idea 6: Rebellious Legacy

The War of the Bloody Gem was a major event in our history where the Diamond King rebelled against the High King of Aul-Dwarov, due to the introduction of the Ruby Gem to the Dwarovkron. The arrogance of Amldihr to introduce a gem of outsiders was intolerable This act caused a brutal civil war which devastated the Dwarovar and left our king exiled, but the High King of Amldihr dead. Their betrayal will never be forgiven and our historical cause will be seen as righteous.

Effects: Land force limit modifier: +15%.

Idea 7: Legacy of Queen Halkraz the Defiant

Known as 'the Defiant' to her subjects and 'the Irksome' to her peers, Queen Halkraz reigned for over 150 years during the early days of Aul-Dwarov. Clashing with the authority of the High King, Halkraz dedicated her life to tirelessly leading the main opposition in the High Assembly. She was a staunch champion for the interests of Arg-Ôrdstun above all else and pushed many beneficial policies through the Amlharaz during her rule.

Effects: Maximum absolutism: +10.

Ambition: Diamond Ambition

Effects: Reserves organisation: +10%.

Aul-Dwarov (I24) — Dwarovic Ideas

Traditions: Dwarovic Traditions

Effects: Leader siege: +1; Fort defense: +15%.

Idea 1: The Dwarovkron

The Dwarovkron is the greatest symbol of Dwarven Unity. It is forged of Kronium, a metal artificially created for the crown, with the specific purpose of being the heaviest metal in existence to physically drive home the weight of rule.

Adorning it are the seven great gems of the Dwarovkron: the Citrine of Seghdihr, the Diamond of Arg-Ôrdstun, the Jade of Grônstunad, the Sapphire of Dûr-Vazhatun, the Agate of Ovdal Asra, the Amethyst of Hul-az-Krakazol, and the Ruby of Ovdal Vudi -- more commonly known as Rubyhold. While other gems do appear on the crown, collectively they all fail to compare to the majesty of even a single of these brilliant stones. And each single stone pales before the majesty of the entire crown.

Effects: Maximum absolutism effect: +15%

Idea 2: The High King’s Warhost

Before the fall of Aul-Dwarov, her armies were called to banner, or muster, by writ of the High King and the High King alone. Each hold seated on the Amlharaz was to maintain its own standing force to see to the defence of the holds' territories beyond its fortifications, to patrol the Dwarovrod, and to protect the Empire whenever mustered by the High King. When times called for multiple fronts to be fought, the High King would traditionally delegate portions of the armies to either the King of Mithradhûm, the King of Orlazam-az-dihr, or the General-King of Gor Vazumbrog as needed, their loyalty and commitment to the High King being absolute no matter who wore the Dwarovkron.

Effects: Discipline: +5%; Vassal force limit contribution: +50%

Idea 3: Forges and Holds

To build a hold in the Serpentspine requires three necessities in varying degrees. The first is an abundance of resources -- vast quantities of ores and minerals to both support the construction efforts on site, and to export for trade in order to procure any missing materials. Second is a perceived need for an easily defensible home, but with defences well beyond any normal city. The third is time: A proper hold takes decades of planning once the original settlement is constructed. Sewers, ventilation, residential districts, access tunnels for foot and cart traffic, farms, and more. Then, centuries of slowly chiselling away stone, inch by inch, to merely scratch the surface of what one could consider the art of creating a hold. Although many holds were built throughout history, none were more grand than the ones created by a united Aul-Dwarov.

Effects: Development cost: -20%

Idea 4: Uddrik’s Legacy

Udrek the Consolidator was seen as the first High King of Amldihr despite never actually holding the title during his lifetime. Udrek had leveraged his predecessor's burgeoning local hegemony over the nearby holds (earned via clever use of the Serpent's Vale irrigation system) into something more substantial.

With the threat of the Frost Giants to the north and west, and the Fire Giants to the east, in 18,109 BA Udrek gathered several kings of the Northern Serpentspine: Balgrin IV Asra of Ovdal Asra, Dagzvult "the Cryptic'' of Verkal Kozenad, and Kogrik II Steelhand of Haraz Orldhûm in an effort to secure the safety of the Serpent's Vale, and by extension the prosperity of dwarvenkind. Each king swore fealty to Udrek of Amldihr under specific conditions, such as stable and cheap access to the sale of Serpent's Vale grains, an obligation to defend each hold as if they were their own, and most importantly the predecessor to the elective position of High King -- Crowned Defender of All Dwarvenkind.

Effects: Diplomatic reputation: +100% (inherited display; unit conversion unverified; script value: diplomatic_reputation = 1); Diplomatic vassal acceptance: +10

Idea 5: Cave Integration Initiative

Though the dwarves of past Aul-Dwarov claimed dominion over the caves of the Serpentspine, in truth that grasp was always tenuous. Though there were great cavern holdings like the Diamond Mines of Arg-Ôrdstun, and the Cobalt Mines of Orlghelovar, no true directed effort was ever made to wrest full control of the many caverns adjoining the Dwarovrod.

This, as we know today, was a grave mistake: contact between holds could be easily severed, and leaving so much of the Serpentspine outside its rule exacerbated the decline of old Aul-Dwarov. By righting this wrong today, we ensure it can never happen again.

Effects: Governing capacity modifier: +20%

Idea 6: Dwarven Craft

Ancient Aul-Dwarov once created wonders the world had never seen before, and after its fall many thought they would never be seen again, as our people had become prisoners in their own domain, or surface exiles who never knew hearth and hold. But Aul-Dwarov has been reforged, and now we can indeed see those ancient wonders and restore them even beyond their prior glory. From the mighty mithril forges of Mithradhûm, to the great rail yards of Er-Natvir and the mighty cannon foundries of Ovdal Kanzad, we shall see the wonders of those who came before us driven to new heights.

Effects: Goods produced modifier: +10%; Monthly splendor: +1

Idea 7: Many Holds, One Mountain Range

The Role of the High King is, in a way, emblematic of the archetypal dwarf. He must be resolute in decision-making, the firm rock that shelters Aul-Dwarov from the storm that lay beyond his realm. He must be willing to listen to the advice provided by his lesser kings, showing flexibility and understanding, knowing that his rule was determined by those who used to be his peers. He must carry the weight of rule on his shoulders -- with the Dwarovkron a constant reminder. Above all else, he must rule with wisdom -- for when wisdom is ignored, dwarven unity is broken.

The greatest example of this is the War of the Bloody Gem, when the Ruby Gem was added to the Dwarovkron without consideration of the Amlharaz or compensation for the slighted holds afterwards, plunging Aul-Dwarov into its bloodiest civil war in millennia. Let us ensure that such a perilous mistake is never made again.

Effects: Same-continent subject liberty desire: +1000%

Ambition: Dwarovic Ambition

Effects: Infantry fire: +15%.
